paragraphs: Daupler sells a response management system that gives teams the information and tools to respond to service requests and emergencies. Public works, utilities, and service organizations of all sizes are named as the users. The work runs from odor complaints to water main breaks.

The company runs call centers that take intake calls, notify staff about urgent issues, and document noncritical calls for the next day. An automated roster callout feature forms crews without anyone working a phone list by hand. Event detection spots incidents affecting multiple people and stops repeat calls from being dispatched. For outbound messages, the system sends a text or a recorded voice message depending on whether the number is mobile or a landline. The platform sits at the center of existing information systems and combines their data into one view of an incident. Site arrival times and crew check-ins are logged to help make sure crews get back safely.
The company states clients are seeing a 20-75% reduction in callouts. Its pages describe the City of Durham integrating the system with CityWorks.
